penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: Any governance or design-ops solution for this problem requires bespoke consulting or workshop work to diagnose incentive structures and implement process changes — per-company manual effort is unavoidable.

penalties_applied.name: requires_synchronous_human
penalties_applied.reason: Selling to CPOs and engineering managers at product companies requires discovery calls and demos; no self-serve path is evident.

rationale: The pain — UX churn driven by promotion incentives — is real and costs real engineering time, and the buyer (CPO / VP Eng at 10-200 person product companies) is more identifiable than many consumer ideas. However, the solution is fundamentally an organisational design intervention, not a software product: it requires diagnosis calls, custom process rollout, and ongoing reinforcement, making autonomous delivery impossible. There is no self-serve software a Claude factory could ship and run hands-off here. Drop.
solution_plan: Not recommended for build. The problem is structural (incentive design) rather than automatable (data processing or content generation), so a Claude factory cannot deliver value without per-company consulting work. Even a lightweight 'UI change governance' dashboard would require integration with each company's Jira/Linear and a change-management process a solo operator cannot run at scale. This is a consulting or coaching product, not a factory-compatible micro-service.
notes: operational_autonomy (2) and buildability_with_ai (3) both fail build_gates; willingness_to_pay (3) and buyer_clarity (5) also fail. Total after penalties (1.1) is far below min_total_to_validate.
